Definition: adverb from a compound of G2095 and a derivative of τείνω (to stretch); in a well-strung manner, i.e. (figuratively) intensely (in a good sense, cogently; in a bad one, fiercely):--mightily, vehemently.
BiblicalUsage: eutónōs means mightily, vehemently. In Luke 23:10, the text says "And the chief priests and scribes stood and vehemently accused him."
TheologicalSignificance: This one, eutónōs, I take at face value: mightily, vehemently.
RelatedEvents: The Crucifixion; Jesus Before Pilate; Jesus Before Herod
